per_frame_issues.c-front (reference): Recognisably the approved character, but the face is slightly wider and flatter, with heavier brows and less refined lip modelling.
per_frame_issues.rest: Identity holds; smile corners and cheek creases look stamped on rather than organically deformed.
per_frame_issues.talk aa (jaw drop): Reads as open A, but the jaw expands into a generic oval with a rubbery lower face and abrupt teeth-to-mouth transitions.
per_frame_issues.talk O (rounded): Reads weakly as O; lips are not sufficiently rounded or projected and the jaw-drop shape remains visible underneath.
per_frame_issues.talk E/ee (spread): Reads clearly, but the exposed teeth form a rigid white strip and the mouth corners pinch unnaturally.
per_frame_issues.talk U (pucker): Pucker reads, but the tiny circular opening and inflated lip ring look doll-like and disconnected from the cheeks.
per_frame_issues.talk m/b/p (closure): Closure reads, though the lips collapse into a thin line and lose the approved character's soft volume.
per_frame_issues.talk f/v (tuck): F/V is ambiguous because the lower-lip-to-teeth contact is too subtle; it reads mostly as a small smile.
per_frame_issues.talk l/t/d (tongue tip): Does not clearly show a tongue tip or alveolar contact; reads as another generic speaking smile.
per_frame_issues.talk ch: Label is not convincing; lip protrusion and compression are insufficient, making it visually redundant with E and L/T/D.
per_frame_issues.listening: Readable and appealing, but the tilt exposes slight eye-size/pupil-tracking inconsistency and stiff hair attachment.
per_frame_issues.thinking: Reads, though the extreme upward gaze and pursed asymmetric mouth feel posed rather than naturally connected.
per_frame_issues.warm: Strong likeness and readable warmth; expression is too close to rest to add meaningful performance range.
per_frame_issues.delight: Readable, but the oversized mouth stretches the cheeks elastically and the teeth/tongue cavity looks pasted in.
per_frame_issues.concern: Reads clearly; brows, eyes and mouth coordinate well, though the lower lip contour is slightly lumpy.
per_frame_issues.surprise: Readable, but repeats the jaw-drop mouth with raised brows rather than supplying a distinct surprised mouth construction.
per_frame_issues.playful: Wink reads, but the closed lid is a flat diagonal slit and the cheek does not convincingly support it.
per_frame_issues.blink frame 1 of the real blink (mid key: Mid-blink is uneven and sleepy-looking; lid arcs and lash silhouettes do not track the eyeballs cleanly.
per_frame_issues.turn yaw -20 (painted plate): Identity weakens: eye scales and facial spacing shift, the nose turns less than the head, and the far cheek feels compressed.
per_frame_issues.turn yaw -10 (blend): Blend is overly frontal; facial features slide laterally without enough volumetric rotation.
per_frame_issues.turn yaw +10 (blend): Eye and mouth placement drift across the face, producing a subtle morph rather than a constructed head turn.
per_frame_issues.turn yaw +20 (painted plate): Major failure at full size: a visible vertical shading/blend seam runs through the brow, nose, cheek and mouth corner; the cheek is smeared and the smile corner is doubled/pinched.
per_frame_issues.roll +8, thinking: Readable, but eye direction, brow deformation and head roll do not feel mechanically unified.
per_frame_issues.yaw +20, delight: Energetic but unstable: the open mouth warps toward the near cheek, facial volume stretches, and the expression no longer matches the approved proportions.

top3_defects: The +20 head-turn plate has a conspicuous vertical blend seam, smeared cheek shading and a malformed/doubled mouth corner.
Head turns are feature-sliding morphs rather than coherent volumetric rotations; eyes, nose, mouth and cheeks change proportions across yaw.
Several visemes are insufficiently differentiated—especially O, U, F/V, L/T/D and CH—and teeth/mouth interiors look rigid or pasted on.
top_fix: Rebuild the head-turn system with clean hand-authored angle plates and angle-specific eyes, nose, mouth and cheek masks; eliminate the +20 seam first, then author genuinely distinct visemes on those stable constructions rather than warping the frontal face.
